title: Prioritize SLO signal fusion and deferred pager policy for capacity-regression events
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
After the capacity regression on 2026-02-10 that caused cascading SLO breaches across serving clusters, we continue to get high-volume low-utility pagers. This ticket implements a combined approach: (1) fuse multi-signal SLO triggers (burn-rate, error-ratio, queue-latency) into a single impact score, and (2) introduce a deferred pager policy that holds paging for low-impact, short-lived spikes while alerting on Slack/ops channels and creating incident records for trend analysis.

Goals:
- Reduce true-duplicate and low-value pages by 60% for capacity-related regressions within 30 days of rollout.
- Keep mean time to detect (MTTD) for high-impact incidents within current SLO limits.
- Provide observability and post-incident artifacts to tune suppression rules.

Approach:
1) Signal fusion: build an Alert Router extension that calculates an "impact score" from normalized signals: burn-rate (weighted 0.45), error-rate (0.35), queue-latency (0.15), and customer-facing-failure-rate (0.05). Impact score maps to action tiers: monitor-only (0.0-0.35), slack-notify (0.35-0.6), elevated-notify (0.6-0.8), page (>=0.8).
2) Deferred paging window: for incidents classified as capacity-regression patterns (sudden throughput drop + KV-cache-miss spike + autoscaler activity), hold pager for a configurable grace period (default 3 minutes) while escalating internal alerts and running automated remediation runbooks. If impact score grows or persists past the window, escalate to page.
3) Graded suppression & hysteresis: apply decay to transient burn spikes using exponential decay (half-life tunable) so single short spikes do not immediately page.
4) Incident-aware quarantine: when a known ongoing incident is detected, automatically apply broader suppression on similar downstream alerts and tag suppressed alerts with incident id for visibility.

Metrics to monitor:
- Pager count per service per week (baseline vs. post-rollout)
- Fraction of alerts suppressed that later required paging (false suppression rate)
- Time-to-page for high-impact incidents
- SLO burn-days and customer-facing error-rate during rollout

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: suppressed critical pager leading to missed major outage. Mitigation: keep page thresholds conservative; require two high-confidence signals to allow suppression; fast path to override suppression from oncall UI.
- Risk: increased complexity and alerting opacity. Mitigation: every suppressed alert will create a lightweight incident record and Slack thread with context and link to metrics used to compute impact score.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration tests verifying impact score mapping and deferred-window timeout behavior exist and pass in CI.
- Canary rollout to two non-critical clusters for 2 weeks with metrics collected and customer_impact not increasing.
- Oncall feedback loop established and documented in runbook.

Notes on scope: this ticket implements the alert-router changes, telemetry dashboards, and runbook updates. Follow-up tickets will train a classifier for incident detection and implement ML-based deduplication.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Unit and integration tests for impact-score and deferred-window pass in CI. 2) Canary rollout does not increase customer-facing error-rate or SLO burn beyond defined guardrails. 3) Pager volume for capacity-pattern incidents reduced >=50% in canary clusters. 4) Runbook and oncall override flows documented and acknowledged by SRE. 5) Post-canary retrospective with data and adjustment plan scheduled.
notes: This ticket intentionally defers ML classifier training and full deduplication; those follow-ups will be created after canary results. We will instrument each suppressed alert with the signals used to compute the score for offline analysis.
